summary: A forum or community home: live counters, the latest discussions with activity, categories, meetups and top helpers, a topics list with sorting and paging, and solved threads with replies.

pages.purpose: Show the community is alive and useful: what it is, the pulse right now, the latest discussions and the ways in.

sections.purpose: A compact header: what the community is for, who it is for, live counters (members, topics, online now) and the join/ask actions.
alternatives: hero: a newer community that needs to explain itself more
fields: Counters: members, topics, solved share, online now
sections.notes: Keep it short so the discussions are above the fold; an 'online now' dot may pulse but respects reduced motion.

sections.purpose: The latest topics, each row with participants, replies, views, a 14-day activity sparkline and time since the last post.
alternatives: list-01: a whole list page with filters and bulk actions
sections.notes: Sort by latest, hot (most posts in 7 days), top (most liked) or unanswered. Each sparkline needs a text equivalent (e.g. the reply count); every cell carries its own label for screen readers.

sections.purpose: Sidebar of categories with topic counts.
fields: Category name, description and topic count
Meetup title, date, time, place or online link

sections.purpose: Top helpers this month, to reward contribution.
fields: Member display name, avatar and accepted answers

pages.purpose: Browse every topic by category, sort and page through them.

sections.purpose: The topic list with a category rail (deep-linkable), the four sort orders and pagination.
alternatives: filter-bar: many tags and filters beyond categories
sparkline: a per-topic activity bar beside the counts
sections.notes: Category links are anchors (#cat-id) so a filtered view can be shared.

pages.purpose: One discussion: the question, the accepted answer marked, replies with likes and quoting, and a reply box.

sections.purpose: Topic title, category, tags and solved state.
The posts with author card, relative time, quoted text, accepted answer and a like toggle per post, then the reply box.
fields: Post author display name and avatar
sections.notes: Like and reply results are reported through a status region. Show the accepted answer near the top as well as in place.

sections.purpose: Sidebar with the thread's pulse: participants, views, created and last-reply times, related topics.

content: Community name, purpose and who it is for
Forum software or data source the pages read from
Sign-up/login method and what membership requires
Rules for showing member names and avatars
Seed topics and accepted answers for launch

styles.name: dense workshop
styles.why: System fonts, compact rows and a warm accent; fast to read for maker, user and open-source communities.

styles.name: dark developer
styles.why: Dark, code-friendly look for developer and product communities.

pitfalls: Sparklines and counters without text equivalents.
Heavy motion on a reading-heavy site; keep transitions quick and honour reduced motion.
No visible guidelines, reporting or moderation path.
Showing members' real names, emails or locations without consent.
An empty-looking launch; seed real topics and answers before going live.
Live counters ('online now') that are fake or never update.
